sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the slow English podcast. My name is Emily. I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Naru. Naru is a tiny island country in the Pacific Ocean.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English. Are you ready? Let's begin. Where is Naru?
Naru is in the Pacific Ocean. It is part of Oceania, northeast of Australia.
It is one of the smallest countries in the world, only 21 square kilometers.
It is a coral island surrounded by blue sea. What is the capital of Naru?
Naru has no official capital city, but most government offices are in a district
called Yarin. Yarin is where the airport, schools, and parliament are. Other districts include
Ayuobuata denigamodu. There are 14 districts in total. How many people live in Naru?
Only about 10,000 people live in Naru. It is the third smallest country by population.
Most people live near the coast, not in the center of the island.
What language do people speak in Naru?
People speak Naru in the local language.
Many also speak English, which is used in schools, business, and government.
Most people are bilingual.
What is the weather like in Naru?
Naru has a tropical climate. It is hot and humid all year.
There are two main seasons, a wet season from November to February,
a dry season from March to October.
Rain helps the island stay green, but the center is often dry and rocky.
What does Naru look like?
Naru has a flat coastline with palm trees, a central plateau with old phosphate mines,
beaches, lagoon areas, and coral reefs. The island is small but has natural beauty.
What animals live in Naru? Because Naru is small, it has few animals,
but you can see sea birds, like forget birds and turns, lizards, insects, and crabs,
fish, octopus, and shellfish in the ocean.
The sea around Naru is good for fishing and diving.
What do people eat in Naru? Naru and food is a mix of local and imported food.
People eat fish, chicken, and pork, rice, instant noodles and potatoes, coconut,
breadfruit, and bananas. Popular foods include grilled fish with rice,
fried chicken with noodles, coconut desserts,
tinned meat, and vegetables.
Because Naru imports many goods, canned and packaged food are common.
What do people drink in Naru? People drink water, tea, and instant coffee,
soft drinks like cola or juice, coconut water, fresh and natural.
Clean drinking water can be a challenge, so rain water is collected in tanks.
What is life like in Naru? Life in Naru is quiet, slow, and close to family.
People enjoy spending time at home, fishing and walking by the sea,
watching TV or playing sports, going to church, sharing meals with family and neighbors.
Many people work for the government or in schools, and some work at the airport or shops.
What are some holidays and traditions in Naru? Independence Day, January 31st,
Constitution Day, May 17th,
Ongum Day, October 26th celebrates the survival of the Naru and people.
Christmas and New Year, church festivals and family events,
people celebrate with music, dancing, food, and games. Some fun facts about Naru.
Naru is the smallest island country in the world. It was once very rich from phosphate mining.
There are no rivers and most water comes from rain or desalination. Cars and trucks drive
around the whole island in under one hour. Naru does not have an army. Now you know many things
